summary.countMethod: Overlapping 37 body, 74 question, 73 formula-card and 531 glossary review groups, not distinct atomic facts. Corrections are 28 thematic groups across 61 independently edited locations, including format and alias fixes.

corrections: Fixed overstrong RRC_IDLE promotion, radio energy and session-anchor glossary guarantees; separated resource-block frequency width from transmission time allocation.
Separated ordinary Wi-Fi ACK policy from all-frame/all-group guarantees; CTS reservation denotes remaining time, not an unchanged RTS duration.
Removed false promises of perfect packet-spraying balance, flowlet ordering under arbitrary delays, permanently low DCTCP queues, and always overflowing microbursts.
Qualified exact VXLAN MTU assumptions, tracked security-group responses and broader current PrivateLink models.
The 655 ms cellular backlog illustration now uses exactly 0.655 seconds and 655,000 bytes; the old 0.65 value was described inaccurately as a rounding of 655 ms.
The PMTU question card no longer claims two ICMP outcomes alone prove a path-MTU interval.
An OpenFlow trace no longer guesses controller intent or labels a priority policy a bug without requirements.
All formula products and compound divisors grouped where needed; unit substitutions improved and a DCTCP worked example is now a standalone defined formula card.
Four non-200 DOI/publisher dictionary reading links replaced with accessible original-paper copies.

The radio-state diagram still equated connected with fast/high power and idle with no radio resources. It now shows RRC context and DRX on an explicitly simplified setup/release path, consistent with the prose.
CTS duration now explicitly means the remaining protected exchange rather than an unchanged RTS duration.
The modulo-remapping explanation now states removal of the last-labelled member before using an equal-remainder proof; the question and physical-label model agree.
Scheduling-request aliases incorrectly resolved to the grant assigning resources. A separate sourced Scheduling request entry now distinguishes asking from receiving permission.
Multi-Link Operation no longer requires links in different bands; modes and hardware constrain concurrency.
SIFS was called the shortest gap in all Wi-Fi. It is now defined by immediate-reply use and its relation to DIFS under the supplied PHY example.
MPDU omitted its frame check sequence. Its definition now includes header, any body and FCS.
Combined OFDMA/MU-MIMO, eNodeB/gNodeB and S-GW+P-GW aliases no longer collapse different mechanisms or components into one definition; PDU no longer aliases an entire PDU session.
Virtualisation is defined as resource abstraction with NFV as an example; NSA wording is scoped to common option 3 rather than all non-standalone architectures.
Tail time no longer aliases tail energy: a duration is not an energy measurement.
Leaf-spine definitions now state the fully connected different-leaf model and distinguish equal topology from configured equal routing cost.
Non-blocking now distinguishes strict circuit non-blocking from rearrangeable and packet-fabric claims.
Switch buffers and microbursts no longer guarantee that every shallow buffer overflows or every deep buffer creates delay.
A VLAN identifier is 12 bits within the tag; the whole IEEE 802.1Q tag is not a 12-bit tag.
Generic P4 match-action processing no longer resolves as an OpenFlow-specific highest-priority table; a distinct generic entry covers the abstraction.
OpenFlow fast failover selects the first live action bucket, whose watch can involve ports or groups, rather than simply the first live port.
ICMPv6 Packet Too Big and MTU black-hole definitions now distinguish classic error-based discovery from possible packetization-layer recovery.
VPN no longer universally means an encrypted tunnel; private logical connectivity and cryptographic confidentiality are distinct.
RACK-TLP now says a tail-loss probe may send new data or retransmit the highest-sequence segment, rather than always retransmitting the last segment.
TLS round-trip claims now describe ordinary full handshakes and account for resumption, early data and retries.
Hosts-file resolution order is configurable; DNSSEC authenticates validated data and denial rather than encrypting or making all data correct.
BGP hijack wording now concerns authorisation rather than mere ownership of a prefix.
Unrepeatered no longer aliases an optical amplifier; generic DC no longer aliases submarine high-voltage shore feeding.

Fibre signal-envelope delay now explicitly uses effective group index rather than generic phase refractive index; the unchanged 1.47 numerical model is supported by Corning’s dated 1.4682 characterisation.
An isotropic antenna is now a separate ideal reference concept rather than an alias for antenna gain.
Ground-station and bent-pipe definitions no longer require large antennas, public Internet service or a geographically nearby user gateway.
Renumbering now allows staged old/new addresses instead of claiming every device and dependency must change simultaneously.
Local formula indices are defined explicitly, inline modulo pseudocode is natural-language wording, and acronym capitalisation is repaired in short-unit introductions.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: A Wi-Fi 7 feature that lets one device associate with an access point over links in more than one band (e.g. 5 and 6 GHz) and use them together or switch between them, depending on mode and hardware.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: A Wi-Fi 7 mechanism coordinating multiple links of multi-link devices, for example across 5 and 6 GHz. Links need not be in different bands, and simultaneous transmission/reception or link switching depends on the supported mode and hardware.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Short interframe space: the shortest Wi-Fi gap, used before an immediate reply such as an ACK or CTS (16 µs on 5 GHz OFDM). Being shorter than DIFS gives these replies priority.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Short interframe space: a Wi-Fi gap before immediate responses such as ACK or CTS, 16 microseconds for the 5 GHz OFDM example. It is shorter than DIFS and gives a sensed immediate reply priority over ordinary DCF contention; it is not the shortest gap in every 802.11 mode.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: MAC protocol data unit: one Wi-Fi MAC frame, header plus payload. Several MPDUs can be aggregated into an A-MPDU.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: MAC protocol data unit: a Wi-Fi MAC frame containing its MAC header, any frame body and a frame check sequence. Component MPDUs can be carried in an A-MPDU.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Interference from a transmitter on an overlapping or neighbouring channel. Its energy can corrupt frames without being decodable, so the networks cannot coordinate.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Interference from transmissions on overlapping or neighbouring channels. Undecodable energy can corrupt frames or trigger energy-based deferral; useful coordination and the resulting performance depend on frequency separation, received power, filtering and equipment.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.
OFDMA and MU-MIMO are distinct multi-user mechanisms; a combined phrase must not resolve solely as MU-MIMO.
The combined LTE/NR phrase must not be defined only as a 5G gNodeB.
The combined gateway pair must not be defined as just the serving gateway.
A protocol data unit is not the same concept as a PDU session association.
A request for resources is distinct from the grant assigning them.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Running a function as software on shared general-purpose hardware instead of on a dedicated box, e.g. mobile-core functions or virtual networks.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Presenting abstracted computing, storage or network resources instead of exposing the underlying physical resources directly. Network-function virtualisation implements functions such as mobile-core components in software on suitable virtualised infrastructure.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Non-standalone 5G: NR radio added alongside an LTE anchor. In the common option 3, LTE and the EPC core handle control, so 5G-core features like slicing are absent.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Non-standalone mobile-system deployment terminology. Common 5G option 3 uses an LTE master and EPC with secondary NR access, so it lacks the 5GC-defined slice/session framework. Other non-standalone options exist; the label alone does not specify the complete architecture.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Energy a phone's radio spends staying in a high-power state after a transfer ends, until inactivity timers move it to a lower-power state.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Additional energy associated with radio activity that persists after payload transfer. Inactivity timers, discontinuous reception, protocol states and other work affect the cost; elapsed tail time is a duration rather than an energy measurement.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.
Time and energy are different physical quantities; tail time should not resolve as energy.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: A two-tier data-centre topology in which every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, so any two racks are three switches apart with one equal path per spine.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: A data-centre switching topology with leaf and spine tiers. In the fully connected two-tier model, every leaf connects to every spine, and different-leaf traffic crosses leaf, spine, leaf with one path per spine. Equal routing cost additionally requires suitable configured costs.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: A switching network is non-blocking if any idle input can always be connected to any idle output without rearranging existing connections.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: In the strict circuit-switching sense, any idle input can connect to any idle output without rearranging established connections. Rearrangeably non-blocking designs permit rearrangement; for packet fabrics a port ratio alone does not prove every traffic matrix can be carried.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Memory in a switch or router that holds packets waiting for an output port. Shallow buffers drop bursts; deep ones add delay.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Memory that holds packets waiting for switch or router service. A burst that exceeds available queue capacity can cause loss; sustained occupancy adds delay. Buffer allocation, queue policy and the traffic pattern determine the outcome.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Virtual LAN: a layer 2 network separated from others on the same switches by a 12-bit tag, giving 4,094 usable IDs.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Virtual LAN: a logical layer-2 network separated from others on shared switching infrastructure. An IEEE 802.1Q tag contains a 12-bit VLAN identifier; values 1 through 4094 identify ordinary VLANs, while 0 and 4095 have reserved meanings.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.
A network and its maximum packet size are distinct concepts; allow underlay and MTU to link separately.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: An OpenFlow group that forwards via the first live port in its list, switching to a backup locally when a link fails, without the controller.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: An OpenFlow group selecting the first live action bucket. Bucket liveness depends on configured watched ports or groups and supported failure detection; preinstalled buckets allow suitable local failover without a controller round trip.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: The ICMPv6 error a router sends when a packet is larger than the next link's MTU; IPv6 routers never fragment, so senders depend on it for PMTUD.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: An ICMPv6 error reporting that a packet exceeds the next-hop link MTU. IPv6 routers do not fragment forwarded packets. Classic IPv6 PMTUD uses this feedback; packetization-layer probing can provide an alternative recovery mechanism.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: A path where large packets are silently dropped because the ICMP 'too big' messages that would tell the sender to shrink them are blocked. Small requests work; large transfers hang.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: A packet-size-dependent failure in which oversized packets are dropped without usable feedback allowing the sender to reduce their size. Blocked ICMP too-big messages are a common cause; stack probing or black-hole detection can prevent a persistent stall.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Virtual private network: an encrypted tunnel carrying private traffic across another network. The added headers reduce the MTU available inside.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Virtual private network: logical private connectivity across shared infrastructure. Some VPNs use encrypted tunnels, while provider-managed VPNs need not provide cryptographic confidentiality. Encapsulation can reduce the inner packet-size budget.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: RACK (Recent ACKnowledgment) detects TCP losses by time rather than counts, and TLP (tail loss probe) resends the last segment early, so lost tails need not wait for an RTO (RFC 8985).
independentCorrectionLedger.after: RACK uses acknowledgment timing to infer TCP losses while accounting for reordering. TLP sends a tail-loss probe that can contain new data or retransmit the highest-sequence segment, potentially eliciting an ACK and avoiding an RTO; success is not guaranteed.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: The exchange that sets up a TLS session: agree versions and keys and verify certificates. TLS 1.3 needs one round trip; TLS 1.2 typically two.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: The exchange that negotiates TLS parameters and establishes traffic keys and peer authentication as configured. An ordinary full TLS 1.3 handshake uses one round trip; common full TLS 1.2 exchanges use two. Resumption, early data, retries and authentication choices change the details.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: A local file mapping names to addresses that the OS checks before (or instead of) DNS.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: A local mapping of hostnames to addresses, such as /etc/hosts. Whether and when an application consults it relative to DNS depends on the configured name-service order and the APIs the application uses.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: DNS Security Extensions: digital signatures on DNS records that let resolvers verify answers have not been tampered with.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: DNS Security Extensions: signatures and a chain of trust allow a validating resolver to authenticate DNS data and authenticated denial of existence. This does not encrypt queries, make every domain signed or guarantee that authorised data is operationally correct.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: Announcing IP prefixes you do not own (often more specific ones) so traffic for them is drawn to you.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: Advertising routing reachability without the relevant authorisation, potentially attracting traffic for another network. Ownership alone is not the test: an owner may authorise another origin, and attacks may also manipulate AS-path information.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: A device that boosts light in a fibre without converting it to electricity; long submarine cables have amplifiers (repeaters) every several tens of kilometres, powered from shore.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: A device that amplifies an optical signal without first regenerating its data electrically. Long-haul repeatered submarine systems use shore-powered optical amplification at design-specific intervals; unrepeatered systems do not contain those submerged repeaters.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.
Unrepeatered is the opposite of having submerged repeaters; it must not define an optical amplifier.
Direct current is a general electrical quantity, not necessarily a submarine-cable high-voltage feed.

independentCorrectionLedger.before: How much slower light travels in a material than in a vacuum. Fibre glass is about 1.47, so light there travels at about 204,000 km/s.
independentCorrectionLedger.after: The phase refractive index compares vacuum light speed with phase velocity in a material. Signal-envelope propagation uses an effective group index, which also depends on wavelength and fibre design; the supplied fibre-delay model uses 1.47.
independentCorrectionLedger.reason: Correct or qualify the definition against the primary source.
